claim: The Drosophila olfactory system contains approximately 58 types of primary sensory neurons that detect chemical, thermal, and hygrosensory stimuli in the third segment of the antenna, arista, and maxillary palp.
source: In Drosophila, the ~58 types of primary sensory neurons that detect these cues are found in the third segment of the antenna, a branched structure emanating from the antenna called the arista, and the maxillary palp (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and references Figure 1A for visual support.

claim: The majority of neurons in the Drosophila antenna are olfactory receptor neurons (ORNs) that respond to volatile compounds.
source: The majority of neurons in the antenna are olfactory receptor neurons (ORNs) that respond to a variety of volatile compounds (Hallem et al., 2004; Hallem and Carlson, 2006; Silbering et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by citations to previous research.

claim: A subset of neurons in the Drosophila antenna and arista respond to temperature and humidity-related stimuli.
source: A subset of neurons in the antenna and arista respond to temperature and humidity-related stimuli (Yao et al., 2005; Ni et al., 2013; Barbagallo and Garrity, 2015; Enjin et al., 2016; Knecht et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by multiple citations.

claim: Each of the approximately 52 types of antennal sensory neurons expresses a distinct sensory receptor or a unique combination of 2-3 receptors.
source: Each of the ~52 types of antennal sensory neurons expresses a distinct sensory receptor, or a unique combination of 2–3 receptors (Couto et al., 2005; Fishilevich and Vosshall, 2005; Goldman et al., 2005; Silbering et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Neurons that express the same receptor(s) project their axons to the same glomerulus of the antennal lobe in the brain.
source: Neurons that express the same receptor(s) also project their axons to the same glomerulus of the antennal lobe in the brain (Couto et al., 2005; Fishilevich and Vosshall, 2005; Benton et al., 2009; Silbering et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by citations.

claim: ORN axons form one-to-one connections with the dendrites of second-order projection neurons (PNs), creating discrete and anatomically stereotyped information-processing channels.
source: Here, their axons form one-to-one connections with the dendrites of second-order projection neurons (PNs), thus creating discrete and anatomically stereotyped information-processing channels (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 1A showing the schematic of the olfactory system.

claim: The study profiled 1,198 high-quality ORNs at 24 hr APF using scRNA-seq.
source: Following quality filtering for cells/nuclei with ≥ 50,000 reads that express at least two out of five neuronal markers (see Materials and methods), we obtained 1,198 and 1,891 high-quality neurons at 24 hr APF and adult, respectively (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text with reference to a figure supplement.

claim: The study profiled 1,891 high-quality ORNs in adults using snRNA-seq.
source: Following quality filtering for cells/nuclei with ≥ 50,000 reads that express at least two out of five neuronal markers (see Materials and methods), we obtained 1,198 and 1,891 high-quality neurons at 24 hr APF and adult, respectively (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text with reference to a figure supplement.

claim: Together with 1,016 ORNs from 42 hr APF, the study profiled a total of 4,105 neurons representing three distinct developmental stages.
source: Together with the 1,016 ORNs from 42 hr APF (Li et al., 2020), we profiled a total of 4,105 neurons, representing three distinct developmental stages (Figure 1B).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text with a citation to previous work.

claim: High-quality ORNs expressed neuronal markers and the antennal cell marker pebbled (peb), but did not detect the glial marker reversed polarity (repo).
source: Confirming transcriptomic quality, we observed high expression of neuronal markers, and the antennal cell marker pebbled (peb), but did not detect the glial marker reversed polarity (repo) in cells at all three stages (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 1—figure supplement 1B showing marker expression.

claim: Transcriptomes could be readily separated into their respective developmental stages following unbiased clustering using differentially expressed genes identified from all stages.
source: Transcriptomes could be readily separated into their respective developmental stages following unbiased clustering using differentially expressed genes identified from all stages (Figure 1D).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 1D showing stage separation.

claim: miple1 is expressed in 24 hr and 42 hr APF ORNs and has known expression in the developing central nervous system.
source: We observed stage-specific expression of select genes such as miple1 in 24 hr and 42 hr APF ORNs (Figure 1E), which has known expression in the developing central nervous system (Celniker et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text, supported by Figure 1E, and includes a citation to previous research.

claim: Adult-specific expression of the olfactory co-receptor Orco was detected.
source: Further, we detect adult-specific expression of the olfactory co-receptor Orco (Larsson et al., 2004; Figure 1F).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text, supported by Figure 1F, and includes a citation.

claim: Substantial transcriptomic changes occur as ORN development proceeds.
source: These data demonstrate the reliability of our single-cell and single-nucleus RNA-seq protocols and suggest that substantial transcriptomic changes occur as development proceeds.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the observed stage-specific gene expression patterns.

claim: When aligning sequencing reads to exons only, both the number of mapped reads and genes detected in ORN nuclei were reduced compared to cells.
source: When we aligned sequencing reads to exons only, both the number of mapped reads and genes detected in ORN nuclei were reduced compared to cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B,C).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by figure supplements showing the comparison.

claim: Intronic reads comprised 32.7% and 26.2% of total reads in 24 hr APF and adult ORN nuclei, respectively, compared to 10.5% in 24 hr APF cell reads.
source: We tested if aligning nuclear sequencing reads to exons and introns could increase the gene detection rate, since intronic reads comprised 32.7% and 26.2% of total reads in 24 hr APF and adult ORN nuclei, respectively, compared to 10.5% when included in 24 hr APF cell reads (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The claim is directly stated with specific percentages and supported by a figure supplement.

claim: Inclusion of intronic reads increased average gene detection rate in nuclei.
source: Indeed, inclusion of intronic reads increased average gene detection rate in nuclei (Figures 2B, C Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by multiple figures.

claim: Including intronic reads in snRNA-seq data provides additional information that is not captured by exonic reads alone.
source: Thus, including intronic reads in snRNA-seq data provides additional information that is not captured by exonic reads alone.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data showing increased gene detection with intronic reads.

claim: More than 70% of genes detected in ORN or PN cells were found in their nuclear counterparts, and more than 90% of nuclear genes were detected in cells.
source: More than 70% of genes detected in ORN or PN cells were found in their nuclear counterparts, and more than 90% of nuclear genes were detected in cells (Figure 2K–L), indicating that snRNA-seq can detect similar genes to scRNA-seq.
evidence: The claim is stated with specific percentages and supported by figures showing Venn diagrams.

claim: Cellular transcriptomes were enriched for genes in GO categories such as translation, protein folding, and metabolic processes, whereas nuclear transcriptomes contained terms related to stage-specific processes.
source: Indeed, cellular transcriptomes were enriched for genes in GO categories such as translation, protein folding, and metabolic processes, whereas nuclear transcriptomes contained terms related to stage-specific processes (Figure 2—figure supplement 1K,L).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by figure supplements showing GO analysis results.

claim: Developing (24 hr APF) transcriptomes were enriched for terms that describe axon and tissue development, cell adhesion, and cell recognition.
source: Developing (24 hr APF) transcriptomes were enriched for terms that describe axon and tissue development, cell adhesion, and cell recognition (Figure 2M,N).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by figures showing GO analysis.

claim: Adult specific-genes were involved in processes like signaling, cell communication, and chemosensory behavior.
source: Adult specific-genes, on the other hand, were involved in processes like signaling, cell communication, and chemosensory behavior (Figure 2M,N).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by figures showing GO analysis.

claim: As ORNs mature, there is a switch in expression from genes important for axon guidance and circuit formation to genes that mediate neuronal signaling and odorant detection.
source: These results indicate that as ORNs mature, there is a switch in expression from genes important for axon guidance and circuit formation to genes that mediate neuronal signaling and odorant detection.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the GO analysis comparing developmental and adult transcriptomes.

claim: ORNs use three distinct families of chemoreceptors to detect olfactory stimuli: Ors (odorant receptors), Irs (ionotropic receptors), and Grs (gustatory receptors).
source: ORNs use three distinct families of chemoreceptors to detect olfactory stimuli: Ors (odorant receptors), Irs (ionotropic receptors), and Grs (gustatory receptors) (Clyne et al., 1999; Vosshall et al., 1999; Scott et al., 2001; Benton et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Chemosensory receptor genes are gradually turned on in the pupal stage, and by adulthood, each neuron type expresses one or few specific receptor(s).
source: These chemoreceptor genes are gradually turned on in the pupal stage; by the time they reach adulthood, each neuron type expresses one or few specific receptor(s) (Figure 3A).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 3A showing the schematic.

claim: Some ORNs began to express chemosensory receptors as early as 24 hr APF.
source: Our scRNA-seq data indicated that some ORNs began to express chemosensory receptors as early as 24 hr APF (Figure 3B).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 3B showing receptor expression.

claim: By 42 hr APF roughly one-third of ORNs expressed Ors.
source: Focusing on the Or family, we found that by 42 hr APF roughly one-third of ORNs expressed Ors (Figure 3C,D).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by figures showing Or expression.

claim: Of the 298 Or-expressing ORNs at 42 hr APF, 84% expressed only one receptor and 16% express two or three.
source: Of the 298 Or-expressing ORNs at 42 hr APF, 84% expressed only one receptor and 16% express two or three (Figure 3D).
evidence: The claim is stated with specific percentages and supported by Figure 3D.

claim: Or85c was detected to be co-expressed with Or85b in 4% of Or-expressing ORNs.
source: Prior to this study Or85c was only reported to be expressed in the larval olfactory system (Kreher et al., 2005), but we detect co-expression of Or85c with Or85b in 4% of Or-expressing ORNs (Figure 3D).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text with a specific percentage, supported by a figure, and includes a citation to previous research.

claim: The majority of developing ORNs express only one Or gene.
source: We conclude that the majority of developing ORNs express only one Or gene.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data showing that 84% of Or-expressing ORNs express only one receptor.

claim: In fewer than 13% of antennal lobes examined, additional labeling outside of the normally innervated glomerulus was observed in permanent labeling experiments.
source: In fewer than 13% of antennal lobes examined, we observed additional labeling outside of the normally innervated glomerulus (Figure 3E, Figure 3—figure supplement 1B–D').
evidence: The claim is stated with a specific percentage and supported by figures.

claim: In the vast majority of cases, permanently labeled ORN axons projected to the same glomerulus as the standard labeled controls, indicating that these Ors were not expressed in multiple ORN types during development.
source: Thus, in the vast majority of cases, permanently labeled ORN axons projected to the same glomerulus as the standard labeled controls (Figure 3E–H), indicating that these Ors were not expressed in multiple ORN types during development.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by figures showing labeling experiments.

claim: Drosophila and mouse ORNs appear to use different strategies for selecting specific olfactory receptor expression.
source: Drosophila and mouse ORNs, therefore, appear to use different strategies for selecting specific olfactory receptor expression (Figure 3I).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from comparing the data with previous research on mouse ORNs.

claim: Olfactory receptor expression is stably maintained across development in Drosophila.
source: The finding that olfactory receptor expression is stably maintained across development in Drosophila enabled us to use cluster-specific receptor expression to match transcriptomic clusters of developing ORNs to their respective ORN types, which also corresponds to the glomerulus their axons innervate (Couto et al., 2005; Fishilevich and Vosshall, 2005; Silbering et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the permanent labeling experiments and is supported by citations.

claim: When plotted following dimensionality reduction with 500 over-dispersed genes, 24 hr APF transcriptomes were separated into three distinct clusters.
source: When plotted following dimensionality reduction with 500 over-dispersed genes, 24 hr APF transcriptomes were separated into three distinct clusters (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by a figure supplement.

claim: acj6, a transcription factor ubiquitously expressed at 42 hr APF, was enriched in the largest cluster but was absent from the other two clusters at 24 hr APF.
source: acj6, a transcription factor ubiquitously expressed at 42 hr APF (Li et al., 2020), was enriched in the largest cluster but was absent from the other two clusters (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text, supported by a figure supplement, and includes a citation.

claim: Antibody staining confirmed that Acj6 protein was expressed in a subset of pan-neuronal Elav+ nuclei in the third antennal segment at 24 hr APF and was absent in the second antennal segment that contains auditory neurons.
source: Antibody staining confirmed that Acj6 protein was expressed in a subset of pan-neuronal Elav+ nuclei in the third antennal segment at 24 hr APF and was absent in the second antennal segment that contains auditory neurons (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by a figure supplement showing immunofluorescence.

claim: The small acj6-negative cluster expressed hearing-related genes and GO terms, suggesting that this cluster corresponds to auditory neurons.
source: The small acj6-negative cluster expressed hearing-related genes (e.g. iav; Senthilan et al., 2012) and GO terms, suggesting that this cluster corresponds to auditory neurons (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B,D-F).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text, supported by figure supplements, and includes a citation.

claim: The large acj6-negative cluster expressed genes and GO terms relating to neurogenesis and sensory organ development, whereas neurite development and cell signaling were found in acj6-positive cells.
source: The large acj6-negative cluster expressed genes and GO terms relating to neurogenesis and sensory organ development, whereas neurite development and cell signaling were found in acj6-positive cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1F,G).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by figure supplements showing GO analysis.

claim: Transcriptomes at 42 hr APF exhibited highest diversity among the three stages of ORNs profiled.
source: For the three stages of ORNs that we profiled, we found that transcriptomes at 42 hr APF exhibited highest diversity (Figure 4B).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 4B showing transcriptomic similarity.

claim: Using differentially expressed genes from 42 hr APF ORNs in combination with known ORN type-specific antennal sensory receptors enabled clear separation of 24 hr APF transcriptomes when embedded in the UMAP space.
source: Thus, we used differentially expressed genes from 42 hr APF ORNs in combination with known ORN type-specific antennal sensory receptors (Grabe et al., 2016) as the gene set for dimensionality reduction; this enabled us to obtain clear separation of 24 hr APF transcriptomes when embedded in the UMAP space (McInnes et al., 2018; Figure 4—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text, supported by a figure supplement, and includes citations.

claim: MARS separated 24 hr APF transcriptomes into 36 distinct clusters.
source: MARS separated 24 hr APF transcriptomes into 36 distinct clusters (Figure 4—figure supplement 2C), which corresponded well with clusters identified by the density-based HDBSCAN approach (Campello et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text, supported by a figure supplement, and includes a citation.

claim: MARS separated closely related clusters that represent multiple ORN types better than HDBSCAN.
source: However, MARS separated closely related clusters that represent multiple ORN types better than HDBSCAN (Figure 4—figure supplement 2C,D).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by figure supplements comparing clustering methods.

claim: MARS was able to separate two clusters, VM5d and VM5v, in 42 hr APF data that were previously indistinguishable.
source: In fact, MARS was able to separate two clusters, VM5d and VM5v (Figure 4—figure supplement 2E), in our 42 hr APF data that were previously indistinguishable (Li et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text, supported by a figure supplement, and includes a citation.

claim: Cluster-specific expression of six receptors allowed annotation of clusters corresponding to V, DM1, VL1, DL4, VA1v, and DM3 ORN types at 24 hr APF.
source: Cluster-specific expression of six receptors allowed us to annotate clusters corresponding to V (Gr21a-expressing), DM1 (Or42b), VL1 (Ir75d), DL4 (Or85f), VA1v (Or47b), and DM3 (Or47a) ORN types (Figure 4C–E, Figure 4—figure supplement 3A–D).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by figures showing receptor expression.

claim: forkhead (fkh) was expressed in neurons projecting to the V glomerulus at both 24 hr and 42 hr APF.
source: Demonstrating the feasibility of this strategy, forkhead (fkh) was expressed in neurons projecting to the V glomerulus at both 24 hr and 42 hr APF (Figure 4D middle, E, Figure 4—figure supplement 2E; Li et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text, supported by figures, and includes a citation.

claim: Using marker genes, an additional 10 ORN clusters were decoded at 24 hr APF.
source: We identified a set of additional marker genes whose individual or combinatorial expression was sufficient to map ORNs at 24 hr APF to their respective 42 hr APF clusters (Figure 4—figure supplement 2E). Using this approach, we decoded the glomerular identity of an additional 10 ORN clusters (Figure 4E–G, Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by figures.

claim: Two ORN types, VM5d and VM5v, mapped to a single cluster at 24 hr APF, indicating that these cells are highly similar at this stage.
source: Two of these ORN types, VM5d and VM5v, mapped to a single cluster at 24 hr APF (Figure 4E), indicating that these cells are highly similar at this stage.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by a figure.

claim: A total of 21 transcriptomic clusters were mapped to ORN types at 24 hr APF.
source: Collectively, we mapped 16 transcriptomic clusters to 17 ORN types at 24 hr APF. Five additional clusters were mapped to ORN types by matching transcriptomic clusters across development (see Figure 6), bringing total mapped 24 hr APF ORN clusters to 21.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text summarizing the annotation results.

claim: 84% of previously reported antennal sensory receptors were expressed in adult transcriptomes.
source: Using this criterion, 84% of previously reported antennal sensory receptors (Menuz et al., 2014) were expressed in adult transcriptomes (Figure 5C).
evidence: The claim is stated with a specific percentage, supported by a figure, and includes a citation.

claim: Excluding widely expressed co-receptors, more than 80% of adult neurons express a sensory receptor.
source: Excluding widely expressed co-receptors (see Figure 9), more than 80% of adult neurons express a sensory receptor (Figure 5C).
evidence: The claim is stated with a specific percentage and supported by figures.

claim: snRNA-seq and bulk antennal RNA-seq detect largely overlapping receptors.
source: We also compared the sensory receptors detected using snRNA-seq with those observed by bulk antennal RNA-seq (Menuz et al., 2014; Barish et al., 2017) and found that these two technologies detect largely overlapping receptors (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text, supported by a figure supplement, and includes citations.

claim: Adult ORN transcriptomes were divided into 26 clusters using MARS.
source: Using similar methods as described earlier, we found that adult ORN transcriptomes were divided into 26 clusters (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by a figure supplement.

claim: MARS outperformed density-based clustering of adult ORNs.
source: Similar to 24 hr APF, MARS outperformed density-based clustering of adult ORNs (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D,E).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by figure supplements comparing clustering methods.

claim: Using cluster-specific receptor expression, 31 neuron types were mapped to 20 adult transcriptomic clusters.
source: Collectively, we used cluster-specific receptor expression to map 31 neuron types to 20 adult transcriptomic clusters (Figure 5G–H).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by figures.

claim: Cells belonging to the same ORN type at 24 hr and 42 hr APF predominantly clustered together, whereas adult transcriptomes remained distinct.
source: Denoting a high degree of transcriptomic similarity, cells belonging to the same ORN type at 24 hr and 42 hr APF predominantly clustered together, whereas adult transcriptomes remained distinct (Figure 6A,B).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by figures showing clustering across stages.

claim: Automatic matching approach linked six more clusters between 24 and 42 hr APF.
source: Our automatic two-way matching approach linked six more clusters between 24 and 42 hr APF. Two of these clusters corresponded to DM4 and VM3 ORNs and four were unannotated (Figure 6B,D, Figure 6—figure supplement 1A,C).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by figures.

claim: By combining manual and automatic approaches, 17 ORN clusters were matched across all three developmental stages.
source: Altogether, by combining manual and automatic approaches, we matched 17 ORN clusters across all three developmental stages.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text summarizing the matching results.

claim: ORNs that belong to the same sensillar class share more similar transcriptomes than those from other classes at 24 hr APF.
source: Overall, ORNs that belong to the same sensillar class share more similar transcriptomes than those from other classes (Figure 7B), similar to our previous observations at 42 hr APF (Li et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text, supported by a figure, and includes a citation.

claim: DL4 ORNs were more similar to the antennal trichoids that take a dorsolateral trajectory than to the ventromedially-projecting basiconics.
source: Indeed, DL4 ORNs were more similar to the antennal trichoids that take a dorsolateral trajectory than to the ventromedially-projecting basiconics annotated here (Figure 7B).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by Figure 7B showing the dendrogram.

claim: Cell-surface molecules and transcription factors constituted 14% and 25% of the differentially expressed genes used to cluster ORN transcriptomes at 24 hr APF, respectively.
source: We also note that cell-surface molecules and transcription factors, which are important regulators of axon targeting, constituted 14% and 25% (as opposed to less than 6% each in the genome; Figure 8B) of the differentially expressed genes used to cluster ORN transcriptomes, respectively (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A–B).
evidence: The claim is stated with specific percentages and supported by figures.

claim: Similarities in 24 hr APF ORN transcriptomes reflect similarities in axon trajectory, in addition to sensillar class.
source: These data suggest that, in addition to sensillar class, similarities in 24 hr APF ORN transcriptomes reflect similarities in axon trajectory.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the hierarchical clustering analysis.

claim: Neurons within the same sensory structures shared more similar transcriptomes in adults.
source: Similar to the pupal stages, hierarchical clustering with differentially expressed genes indicated that neurons within the same sensory structures shared more similar transcriptomes (Figure 7C, Figure 7—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by figures.

claim: Adult transcriptomes also reflected the type of stimuli they detect.
source: A closer examination revealed that adult transcriptomes also reflected the type of stimuli they detect.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the hierarchical clustering analysis of adult neurons.

claim: DC1 ORNs from the trichoid at3 sensillum sense limonene and their transcriptomes were more similar to fruit odor-responsive basiconic ORNs than to the pheromone-detecting trichoid ORNs.
source: DC1 ORNs from the trichoid at3 sensillum, for instance, sense limonene (Dweck et al., 2013) and their transcriptomes were more similar to fruit odor-responsive basiconic ORNs than to the pheromone-detecting trichoid ORNs (Figure 7A,C).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text, supported by figures, and includes a citation.

claim: 370 and 554 differentially expressed genes were identified between all 24 hr APF and 42 hr APF ORN clusters, respectively.
source: We identified 370 and 554 differentially expressed genes between all 24 hr APF and 42 hr APF ORN clusters, respectively (Figure 8A).
evidence: The claim is stated with specific numbers and supported by a figure.

claim: 42 hr APF ORNs had more differentially expressed genes than their 24 hr APF counterparts, in line with the finding that this mid-developmental stage contained ORNs with the most distinct transcriptomes.
source: The fact that 42 hr APF ORNs had more differentially expressed genes than their 24 hr APF counterparts is in line with our finding that this mid-developmental stage contained ORNs with the most distinct transcriptomes (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from comparing the number of differentially expressed genes and transcriptomic diversity.

claim: The set of differentially expressed genes shared between both developmental stages comprised 211 genes, 170 of which were differentially expressed among the 21 matched ORN types.
source: Next, we defined the set of differentially expressed genes shared between both developmental stages, as this dataset likely contains genes important for ORN development. This list comprised 211 genes, 170 of which were differentially expressed among the 21 matched ORN types (Figure 8A).
evidence: The claim is stated with specific numbers and supported by a figure.

claim: Transcription factors (TFs) and cell-surface molecules (CSMs) were over-represented in the differentially expressed genes shared between 24 hr and 42 hr APF ORNs compared to their genome-wide percentages.
source: Transcription factors (TFs) and cell-surface molecules (CSMs) were over-represented in the differentially expressed genes shared between 24 hr and 42 hr APF ORNs compared to their genome-wide percentages (Figure 8B; Figure 8—figure supplements 1–4).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by figures.

claim: Thirty-four TFs were differentially expressed in the developing ORNs matched between 24 and 42 hr APF.
source: Thirty-four TFs were differentially expressed in the developing ORNs matched between 24 and 42 hr APF.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text.

claim: Some TFs displayed broad expression in nearly all ORN types, including tonali (tna), scribbler (sbb), Distal-less (Dll), 48 related 1 (Fer1), and Ecdysone-induced protein 93F (Eip93F).
source: Some TFs displayed broad expression in nearly all ORN types, including tonali (tna), scribbler (sbb), Distal-less (Dll), 48 related 1 (Fer1), and Ecdysone-induced protein 93F (Eip93F) (Figure 8C), the latter four of which have previously described expression in the antenna (Jafari et al., 2012; Barish et al., 2017; Chai et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text, supported by a figure, and includes citations.

claim: Both Fer1 and Eip93F regulate expression of a subset of Or genes.
source: Both Fer1 and Eip93F regulate expression of a subset of Or genes (Jafari et al., 2012), but our data suggests that they could have additional functions in Ir-positive ORNs (Figure 8C).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text, supported by a figure, includes a citation, and suggests additional functions based on the data.

claim: Fifty-three CSMs were differentially expressed in developing ORNs.
source: We next analyzed CSMs. Fifty-three CSMs were differentially expressed in developing ORNs (Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by a figure supplement.

claim: Many differentially expressed CSMs were members of protein families implicated in circuit assembly, such as Beaten Path (beat), Down Syndrome Cell Adhesion Molecule (Dscam), Fasciclin (Fas), Netrin (Net), Roundabout (robo), Defective Proboscis Extension Response (Dpr), and Semaphorin (Sema).
source: Many of them were members of protein families implicated in circuit assembly, such as Beaten Path (beat), Down Syndrome Cell Adhesion Molecule (Dscam), Fasciclin (Fas), Netrin (Net), Roundabout (robo), Defective Proboscis Extension Response (Dpr), and Semaphorin (Sema; Figure 8—figure supplements 1–3; Kolodkin and Tessier-Lavigne, 2011; Sanes and Zipursky, 2020), suggesting that these differentially expressed CSMs could regulate ORN wiring.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text, supported by figure supplements, and includes citations.

claim: 203 differentially expressed CSMs were identified in six synaptic partner ORNs and PNs at 42 hr APF and 48 hr APF, respectively.
source: Finally, to aid in identification of molecules important for synaptic partner matching, we queried differentially expressed genes in six synaptic partner ORNs and PNs (from the companion manuscript, Xie et al., 2021) at 42 hr APF and 48 hr APF, respectively. From this gene set, we identified 203 differentially expressed CSMs (Figure 8—figure supplements 5, 6).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text, supported by figure supplements, and references a companion manuscript.

claim: In 68% of adult ORN nuclei, Orco was highly expressed.
source: In our adult transcriptomes, 68% of neurons highly expressed Orco (Figure 9—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is stated with a specific percentage and supported by a figure supplement.

claim: Orco was expressed in many Ir and Gr clusters.
source: Although highly enriched in Or-positive ORN clusters, we found that Orco was expressed in many Ir and Gr clusters (Figure 9B; Figure 9—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by figures.

claim: Ir8a expression was restricted to Ir-positive clusters.
source: As previously reported (Silbering et al., 2011), Ir8a expression was restricted to Ir-positive clusters (Figure 9B; Figure 9—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text, supported by figures, and includes a citation.

claim: Ir25a was more highly and broadly expressed in some Or clusters in addition to Ir clusters.
source: However, Ir25a was more highly and broadly expressed in some Or clusters in addition to Ir clusters (Figure 9B; Figure 9—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by figures.

claim: Or and Ir co-receptor transcripts are broadly expressed at the cluster-level.
source: These data indicate that Or and Ir co-receptor transcripts are broadly expressed at the cluster-level.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observed expression patterns of co-receptors.

claim: Orco was co-expressed broadly with cells expressing Ir8a, Ir25a, and Ir76b.
source: Using this criterion, we found that Orco was co-expressed broadly with cells expressing Ir8a, Ir25a, and Ir76b (Figure 9C).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by a figure.

claim: Orco was also expressed in a subset of Gr21a-positive ORNs.
source: In addition to Ir co-receptors, Orco was also expressed in a subset of Gr21a-positive ORNs (Figure 9—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by a figure supplement.

claim: The findings are in line with two recent studies that reveal broad expression and function of Ir and Or co-receptors in Drosophila and mosquitos.
source: Our findings are in line with two recent studies that reveal broad expression and function of Ir and Or co-receptors in Drosophila and mosquitos (Task et al., 2020; Younger et al., 2020).

claim: Expression of Gr64a, Gr64f, and Gr93a was correlated with the expression of a subset of Ors.

claim: Gr64a and Gr64f mediate sugar detection in gustatory neurons.
source: Both Gr64a and Gr64f mediate sugar detection (Dahanukar et al., 2007; Jiao et al., 2008), whereas Gr93a is required for caffeine responses (Lee et al., 2009) in gustatory neurons.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by citations to previous research.

source: Additionally, Gr64f expression was broadly correlated with expression of Ors expressed by basiconic ORNs used to detect food-related odorants, including Or22a/b (DM2-projecting ORNs), Or42b (DM1-projecting ORNs), Or59b (DM4-projecting ORNs), Or92a (VA2-projecting ORNs), and Or9a (VM3-projecting ORNs) (Figure 9—figure supplement 2A).

claim: The expression of Grs in Or-positive ORNs suggests potential functions for them in these cells.

claim: 262 differentially expressed genes were identified between Or- and Ir-positive neurons.
source: To examine this, we first identified 262 differentially expressed genes between Or- and Ir-positive neurons (Figure 10—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is stated with a specific number and supported by a figure supplement.

claim: Many of the differentially expressed genes between Or- and Ir-positive neurons included those important for chemosensory behavior, such as sensory receptors, Sensory neuron membrane protein 1 (Snmp1), and ATPase 8B (ATP8B), as well as TFs and other signaling proteins.
source: In line with previous reports (Menuz et al., 2014; Mohapatra and Menuz, 2019), many of the differentially expressed genes included those important for chemosensory behavior, such as sensory receptors, Sensory neuron membrane protein 1 (Snmp1; Benton et al., 2007), and ATPase 8B (ATP8B; Ha et al., 2014; Liu et al., 2014), as well as TFs and other signaling proteins (Figure 10—figure supplement 1).

claim: Or- and Ir-positive ORNs may utilize distinct genes for their function.
source: These data indicate that Or- and Ir-positive ORNs may utilize distinct genes for their function.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the differentially expressed genes between Or- and Ir-positive neurons.

claim: short neuropeptide F precursor (sNPF), previously reported to regulate olfactory sensitivity of DM1 ORNs, was differentially expressed in adult ORNs.
source: We found that one neuropeptide previously reported to regulate olfactory sensitivity of DM1 ORNs (Root et al., 2011), short neuropeptide F precursor (sNPF), was differentially expressed in adult ORNs (Figure 10A).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text, supported by a figure, and includes a citation.

claim: The fact that sNPF was enriched in multiple ORN types suggests that it could have functions beyond DM1 ORNs.
source: The fact that sNPF was enriched in multiple ORN types suggests that it could have functions beyond DM1 ORNs.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed expression pattern of sNPF.

claim: The clustering methods separated 24 hr APF and adult transcriptomes into 36 and 26 clusters, respectively, and further divided 42 hr APF transcriptomes into 34 clusters.
source: Our clustering methods separated 24 hr APF and adult transcriptomes into 36 and 26 clusters, respectively, and further divided 42 hr APF transcriptomes into 34 clusters.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text summarizing the clustering results.

claim: 16 annotated ORN types were matched across all three developmental stages.
source: We matched 16 annotated ORN types across all three developmental stages.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text summarizing the matching results.

claim: The fact that fewer clusters were observed than the approximately 50 glomerular types could be because not enough cells were profiled for some types, closely related types formed a single cluster, or some Ir-positive neuronal types expressed the same receptor and could not be further subdivided transcriptomically.
source: The fact that we observed fewer clusters than the ~50 glomerular types could be because: (1) not enough cells were profiled for some types; (2) closely related types formed a single cluster (e.g. VM5d and VM5v ORNs at 24 hr APF or VA5 and VM3 ORNs in adults; Figures 4F, 5G); or (3) some Ir-positive neuronal types expressed the same receptor and could not be further subdivided transcriptomically (Figure 5F; Figure 5—figure supplement 2M,P).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text with specific examples and supported by figures.

claim: snRNA-seq can be used to profile cuticle-associated tissues.
source: Single-nucleus RNA-seq can be used to profile cuticle-associated tissues

claim: The advantages of snRNA-seq include: tissue can be kept in long-term storage at –80°C prior to processing; snRNAseq reduces cell-type sampling bias; and nuclei are more easily captured by microfluidics devices than large and/or fragile cells.
source: The advantages of snRNA-seq include: (1) tissue can be kept in long-term storage at –80°C prior to processing (Wu et al., 2019; Ding et al., 2020); (2) snRNAseq reduces cell-type sampling bias (Denisenko et al., 2020); and (3) nuclei are more easily captured by microfluidics devices than large and/or fragile cells (Cui et al., 2020; Denisenko et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by citations to previous research.

claim: High-quality nuclei can be isolated from frozen tissues which allows researchers studying low-abundance cell types to collect and freeze a large amount of tissue over time to ensure that they have an adequate number of nuclei for downstream processing and analyses.
source: Underscoring the utility of this protocol, high-quality nuclei can be isolated from frozen tissues which allows researchers studying low-abundance cell types to collect and freeze a large amount of tissue over time to ensure that they have an adequate number of nuclei for downstream processing and analyses.
evidence: The claim is stated in the text as an advantage of the snRNA-seq protocol.

claim: The scRNA-seq and snRNA-seq protocols detected largely overlapping genes.
source: Critically, we found that our scRNA-seq and snRNA-seq protocols detected largely overlapping genes (Figure 2K,L).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by figures showing Venn diagrams.

claim: snRNA-seq is well-suited for profiling previously inaccessible neurons in the adult fly.
source: Collectively, we demonstrated that snRNA-seq is well-suited for profiling previously inaccessible neurons in the adult fly and this protocol can be easily used by other researchers that want to gain transcriptomic access to their tissue of interest (see a detailed protocol in Materials and methods section).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the comparison of snRNA-seq and scRNA-seq.

claim: The dataset will enable analyses of molecular underpinnings of neural circuit formation, maintenance, and function by providing access to the transcriptomes of anatomically and functionally distinct neuron types at developmentally-relevant stages.
source: Understanding the molecular underpinnings of neural circuit formation, maintenance, and function requires that we can access the transcriptomes of anatomically and functionally distinct neuron types at developmentally-relevant stages. Here, we created a dataset that will enable these types of analyses by profiling Drosophila ORNs at stages corresponding to: (1) initial axon pathfinding (24 hr APF); (2) synaptic partner matching (42 hr APF; Li et al., 2020); and (3) sensory function (adult).
evidence: The claim is stated in the text and supported by a citation.

claim: The abundant differentially expressed transcription factors and cell-surface molecules defined in distinct ORN types at both 24 hr and 42 hr APF are excellent candidates to test as regulators of cell-type-specific axon guidance and target selection.
source: The abundant differentially expressed transcription factors and cell-surface molecules that we defined in distinct ORN types at both 24 hr and 42 hr APF (Figure 8; Figure 8—figure supplements 1–6) are excellent candidates to test as regulators of cell-type-specific axon guidance and target selection.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the identification of differentially expressed genes.

claim: The data suggests that neurons that detect similar cues may require analogous genes for their function.
source: Our data suggests that neurons that detect similar cues may require analogous genes for their function.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that adult transcriptomes reflect sensory stimuli.

claim: The differentially expressed neuronal transmission and signaling genes could provide important insight into the functional properties of distinct ORN types.
source: Furthermore, the differentially expressed neuronal transmission and signaling genes (Figure 10) could provide important insight into the functional properties of distinct ORN types.
evidence: This is a speculation about the potential utility of the identified genes.

source: In conclusion, this work, together our accompanying paper profiling PNs at multiple stages (Xie et al., 2021), should spur novel and important biological discoveries in the fields of sensory system development and function.
